result.text: Title: Ordering in an Online Shop A customer that logs into an E-Shop system and has to wait for its login confirmation (its credentials are checked by the system).
If the login was successful then the customer can continue to select products, else the shopping experience stops.
After selecting a product the customer has to add it to a shopping cart, save the product and check if every product was already selected.
These steps repeat until all products were selected.
Then the order is finished by the shopping system and simultaneously payment and shipment for the order is prepared.
For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant performs its own action on a system (such as logging in or submitting its own input) and that the system then checks that action before a decision depends on the result: Model the participant's own action as a userTask performed by that participant, labeled with the verb and object the description uses for that action, placed in sequence before the system's check task. Do not drop this action or fold it into the check task. Keep any wait for the confirmation after the participant's action and before the process continues.

When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action (an activity it names), rather than when an external message, signal, time or condition occurs: Model a start event for the process beginning, with no incoming flow, followed by a task labeled with that participant's action in the description's own wording. Do not label the start event with the action, and do not replace the action with the start event.

When the description says a participant first checks whether they already have something, and a later exclusive decision branches on the result of that check: Model the check as its own activity performed by that participant, labeled with the description's own wording for the check, placed after the preceding step and before the exclusive gateway that branches on the result. Do not drop the check or fold it into the gateway's label or condition, and do not model it as a gateway.

When the description says that an occurrence (such as a checkpoint being reached) can happen at any point while an ongoing activity is running and that the participant is informed of it, and the description does not state that the occurrence starts the process: Model the occurrence as an intermediate catch event placed in the flow of the running activity, not as a start event and not as a separate subprocess. Route the flow so that the running activity continues after the participant has been informed. If the description states that the occurrence is checked before the participant is informed, place an exclusive gateway before the notification step to decide whether the occurrence has happened. Model the notification step as a task labeled with the description's wording for the notification, or as a send task only when the description states a message being sent.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:userTask for human work assisted by software and bpmn:manualTask for human work performed without an execution application.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Use bpmn:serviceTask for automated service work, bpmn:scriptTask for an explicit script, and bpmn:businessRuleTask for explicit rule evaluation.
